slides.title: ZERO-DAY
slides.subtitle: AI-Based Detection of Cyber Threats in Unidirectional IP Traffic

bullets.text: Smart India Hackathon 2026  •  Problem Statement 26145  •  NTRO
Team ZERO-DAY  |  Dual-Layer Anomaly Detection  |  Read-Only Passive Defence

slides.notes: Good morning faculty. I'm presenting ZERO-DAY, our solution to SIH 2026 problem statement 26145 from NTRO: AI-Based Detection of Cyber Threats in Unidirectional IP Traffic.

slides.title: The Problem in 30 Seconds
slides.subtitle: Critical infrastructure can only watch — never touch.

bullets.text: Power grids, banks & nuclear plants use hardware DATA DIODES to copy traffic into a secured monitoring enclave.
Data flows ONE WAY only  →  the system can SEE everything, but can NEVER probe, re-contact, or block.
This unidirectional blind spot is exactly where attackers hide.
The challenge: detect 6 classes of cyber threat using PURELY PASSIVE observation.

slides.notes: The key insight: data diodes make monitoring highly secure, but the cost is no active interaction. That is the heart of the problem.

slides.title: Why Unidirectional?

shapes.text:
✓  Air-Gap Security

No return path = attackers on the internet can't reach the monitor.

✗  The Trade-off

We lose the ability to respond, probe, or confirm — detection must be passive.
The data diode is a one-way mirror: total visibility, zero accessibility.

slides.notes: Why does the problem even exist? Because unidirectional monitoring is very secure against being attacked, but you pay for it by not being able to interact.

slides.title: Our Solution: Dual-Layer Detection

shapes.text:
LAYER 2  •  NJ-ODE
unsupervised • zero-day • channel attribution

slides.notes: Two layers working together. Layer 1 knows what attacks look like. Layer 2 knows what normal looks like.

slides.title: Layer 1 — Rule-Based Detectors
slides.subtitle: Known attack signatures, matched in milliseconds.

bullets.text: Six detectors on a common interface — DDoS, C2 Beacon, DGA, DNS Tunnel, Port Scan, Exfiltration.
Streaming: each FlowEvent processed one-at-a-time with bounded rolling-window state.
Every alert carries evidence — WHAT (threat class), HOW confident, and WHY (feature + reason).
Fast & explainable: 40,202 events/sec, under 1 ms per event.

slides.notes: Layer 1 is the speed layer. Example: SYN flood detector flags 150 SYN-only packets when the threshold is 100, citing 25 unique source IPs as evidence.

slides.title: Layer 2 — Neural Jump ODE
slides.subtitle: The AI that catches what rules can't.

bullets.text: Unsupervised anomaly detection — trains on BENIGN traffic only, no labels needed.
Learns the continuous-time expectation of normal traffic (Herrera, Krach & Teichmann — ICLR 2021).
Anomaly score = prediction error between expected and observed behaviour.
CHANNEL ATTRIBUTION tells analysts which feature broke (IAT, bytes, entropy, burst, direction) → maps to a threat class.

slides.notes: Layer 2 is the intelligence layer. No attack labels, just a learned model of normal. Deviation = anomaly = possible zero-day.

slides.title: The X-Factor: Zero-Day Detection

shapes.text:
RULES know what ATTACKS look like.

Catch what you've already seen.
Miss everything you haven't.

NJ-ODE knows what NORMAL looks like.

Anything that isn't normal gets flagged — even attacks never seen before.
This is the whole point of AI-based detection: defence against the unknown.

slides.notes: The differentiator. A rule-based system stops at yesterday's attacks. Our second layer flags tomorrow's. That is why AI is justified, not just rules.

slides.title: Threat Coverage — SIH 26145
slides.subtitle: Six classes, dual coverage.

bullets.text: Volumetric / Protocol DDoS — SYN flood + UDP amplification.
Botnet C2 Beaconing — periodic callbacks, detected by IAT periodicity.
DGA Domains — malware generating random domain names via entropy scoring.
DNS Tunnelling — data hidden inside DNS queries (length + record-type anomalies).
Encrypted-Session Malware — TLS metadata behavior, NO decryption.
Reconnaissance / Port Scan & Data Exfiltration — fan-out + volumetric asymmetry.

slides.notes: Cover all six classes with both layers. Rules catch known variants; the model catches deviations on matching feature channels.

slides.title: The Encrypted-Traffic Question
slides.subtitle: We can't see inside — and we never need to.

bullets.text: Hard constraint: TLS/QUIC payloads are never decrypted.
Instead, we analyze TLS METADATA: packet-size coefficient of variation, timing variation, JA3/JA4 fingerprints.
Malicious sessions have a different statistical rhythm than benign ones — even when encrypted.

slides.notes: This is the trap question. We stay on the right side of the constraint by reading metadata, not content. Encryption can't hide statistical behaviour.

slides.title: Measured Performance

shapes.text:
70  evt/s
RULES + NJ-ODE • ~14 ms per event

26 / 26  TESTS PASSING
Streaming, not batch — bounded latency

96 WINDOWS • ~5s TRAIN
NJ-ODE training in 60 epochs

slides.notes: Real measured numbers from our benchmark harness — not estimates. Rules are the speed layer, NJ-ODE the depth layer.

slides.title: Security Properties & PS Compliance

bullets.text: Read-only ingest — no probes, no return path, no inline blocking.
No payload decryption — TLS/QUIC metadata only.
Air-gap compatible — requires no return path.
Evidence chain — every alert carries cited feature values.
Bounded state & thread-safe engine — deque pruning + cooldowns + N-of-M hysteresis → no alert storms.

slides.notes: Every constraint in the problem statement is satisfied by design, and we have the mechanisms to prove it.

slides.title: Validation & Honest Next Steps

bullets.text: Current: synthetic-vs-synthetic evaluation — 100% detection rate across all 6 attack scenarios.
On real data, we're clear: production validation needs CIC-IDS2017 / CSE-CIC-IDS2018.
That real-dataset validation is our clearly-scoped next step.

slides.notes: The honest answer on data. Owning the limitation builds trust — and frames the forward work. Never overclaim evaluation.

slides.title: Tech Stack
slides.subtitle: Built to be fast, correct, and visual.

bullets.text: Python 3.11+  •  PyTorch 2.0+  •  NJ-ODE (continuous-time anomaly model)
Pydantic v2 — strict alert schema with evidence chain
FastAPI + WebSocket — real-time API and alert streaming
React + TypeScript — SOC-style operations dashboard
pytest — 26 passing tests guarding the detection engine

slides.notes: A modern, defensible stack: streaming backend, strict contracts, and a real dashboard a security analyst would use.
